SOFTWARE + MEASUREMENT HARDWARE

Choose the right front end.

This app converts Uno ADC readings using the setup you specify. It cannot detect your wiring, switch measurement circuits, or protect the inputs. A USB-connected Uno shares ground with your computer. Use isolated, low-voltage bench sources only. Do not connect mains, negative voltage, or motor transients directly. No CAT safety rating or guaranteed accuracy is claimed.

DC voltage

For signals in 0–5 V, connect the signal to the selected analog input and its ground to GND. The ADC reference setting must match the actual Uno supply/reference. A reading at full scale can also mean the input exceeds the ADC range.

Higher voltages require an engineered divider and protection: input → R top → analog node → R bottom → GND. Enter (R top + R bottom) / R bottom. Account for resistor tolerances, power dissipation, ADC loading, worst-case voltage, and transient protection. The multiplier is a calculation, not a safe voltage rating. A nominal 12 V motor circuit can have much larger spikes; do not connect it with only an assumed software range.

DC current

Use a suitable analog-output current sensor. The browser computes I = (ADC voltage − zero-current voltage) / sensitivity. Enter the sensor's real zero voltage, sensitivity in V/A, and current rating. The example defaults are not a detected sensor. The current path belongs in the correctly rated sensor circuit, never an Uno analog pin. Add appropriate protection and fusing for the application.

For example, the ACS712 family has several sensitivities and current ranges. Choose the exact part's specification. A component's isolation specification does not make an assembled hobby board safe for mains. I²C-only sensors such as INA219 need a different firmware protocol and are not supported by this analog conversion.

Resistance and continuity

Disconnect the component from power and isolate it from parallel circuit paths. Use Uno 5V → R known → analog input → R unknown → GND, with the default ADC reference tied to the same supply. Enter the actual known resistance. The conversion is R unknown = R known × raw / (1023 − raw). Full-scale is displayed as OL because it may be an open circuit or outside the usable range.

Choose a reference near the expected unknown resistance for useful resolution. Very small and very large values are inaccurate because of lead resistance, input loading, and ADC quantization. Continuity is a visual comparison against the chosen resistance threshold, not a certified continuity tester. It has no audible buzzer. A different external ADC reference requires a different resistance model.

Potentiometer

Connect outer terminals to 5V and GND and the wiper to the selected input. This preset reports electrical position. It does not infer unknown resistance, and a logarithmic potentiometer's mechanical position is not proportional to its voltage ratio.

AC and advanced functions

AC RMS, capacitance, diode testing, frequency, and protected autoranging are not implemented. The 20 Hz sample stream is for slow DC measurements, not waveform analysis. True RMS requires suitable signal conditioning and sampling; diode and capacitance functions need controlled excitation and measurement circuitry. For handheld-multimeter functionality, a protected measurement module or a commercial meter with a documented USB/serial interface is the next hardware step.

Six channels, one selected measurement

The new firmware reads A0–A5 sequentially, not simultaneously. Unconnected channels float and produce meaningless readings. Select only an input that is wired. The browser records and graphs the selected channel. The old sketch's plain integer lines remain supported on A0 only.
